name: Hierarchical Disentanglement Benchmark
description: In representation learning, there has been recent interest in developing algorithms to disentangle the ground-truth generative factors behind a dataset, and metrics to quantify how fully this occurs. However, these algorithms and metrics often assume that both representations and ground-truth factors are flat, continuous, and factorized, whereas many real-world generative processes involve rich hierarchical structure, mixtures of discrete and continuous variables with dependence between them, and even varying intrinsic dimensionality. In this work, we develop benchmarks, algorithms, and metrics for learning such hierarchical representations.
evaluation_method: disentanglement metrics (hierarchical variants of MIG/HSIM, DCI-style scores, reconstruction/log-likelihood reported as auxiliary)
general_score_metric: hierarchical disentanglement score (composite metric based on hierarchical-MIG / proposed hierarchical metrics)
reputation: A research-focused benchmark adopted within the disentanglement/representation-learning community but not broadly used outside that subfield.
notes: Primarily synthetic / procedurally generated datasets with hierarchical factors; metrics can be sensitive to metric choice and implementation; non-LLM, relatively small-scale compared with large vision benchmarks.
